title: Ocean & Ice Animals!
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Milo the bluebird. Welcome back to The Animated Zoo!
Today we're visiting animals from the cold ice and the deep blue sea.
Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!

lines: Here's our first animal. Here's a clue: it's a bird that can't fly! Can you guess?
First, brr! Let's visit the penguins!
Penguins are birds, but they can't fly.
Instead, they swim super fast, using their wings like flippers.
Penguin moms and dads take turns keeping their egg warm.
Can you flap your arms like penguin flippers? Flap, flap!
Can you guess? Do penguins have knees?
Yes! Their knees are hidden up inside their feathers.
That's why penguins waddle, step by step. Can you waddle too?
Who's next? Here's a clue: it lives in the sea and has eight arms! Can you guess?
Now let's dive deep into the ocean to meet the octopus!
An octopus has eight arms, with suckers that help it grab and taste things.
An octopus has no bones, so it can squeeze through tiny spaces.
Can you wiggle your arms like an octopus? Wiggle, wiggle!
Can you guess how many hearts an octopus has?
Three! And its blood is blue.
An octopus can also change its color to hide. Watch!
It's a master of hide and seek!
Who's next? Here's a clue: it carries a shell on its back and swims in the sea! Can you guess?
Swim with me over to the sea turtles!
Sea turtles glide through the ocean with their big flippers.
Sea turtles can live for a very, very long time.
Can you swim like a sea turtle? Paddle, paddle!
Can you guess? Can a sea turtle hide its head inside its shell?
No! Sea turtles can't pull their heads in, like some land turtles can.
Let's say it together: SEA TURTLE!
Mommy sea turtles lay their eggs in the sand on the beach.
When the babies hatch, they crawl all the way to the ocean.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's big and white, and it lives in the snow! Can you guess?
Brr! Let's go back to the snow to see the polar bears!
Polar bears are the biggest bears in the world.
Polar bears have thick fat under their fur, like a cozy blanket.
Can you stomp like a big polar bear? Stomp, stomp!
Can you guess what color a polar bear's skin is?
It's black! Their fur looks white, but the skin underneath is black.
Let's say it together: POLAR BEAR!
Their big, wide paws help them walk on snow and swim in icy water.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's pink, and it likes to stand on one leg! Can you guess?
Our last stop is the flamingo lake. Look at all that pink!
Flamingos live together in big, noisy groups.
Flamingos eat with their heads upside down! Can you tip your head down too?
Can you guess why flamingos are pink?
Because of the food they eat! Tiny shrimp and plants called algae make their feathers pink.
Baby flamingos are gray or white. They turn pink as they grow up.
Flamingos often stand on one leg. Scientists think it may help them rest.
Can you stand on one leg like a flamingo? Let's try!

recap: What a splashy adventure! Let's remember.
Sea turtles can't hide their heads.
And flamingos are pink because of their food!
outro: Which animal was your favorite? Remember, be kind to every animal. Watch quietly and give them space.
Bye, friends! See you at the zoo!
